## On Blank Pages and Blue Hours

The other day, I found an old notebook with nothing inside except a date on the first page. It was dated seven years ago. I don’t remember buying it, or what I planned to write, or why I stopped after one line. But holding it made me feel something like hope—not because I wanted to fill it now, but because it reminded me that there is always a version of ourselves that gets to begin again.

We spend so much time trying to make every moment count. We schedule our mornings, curate our evenings, and measure our days in tasks completed. But the most beautiful things often arrive unannounced: a sudden change in the light, a half-remembered song, a conversation that outlasts its purpose. They don’t ask permission. They simply happen, and then they are gone. The notebook was a small monument to that kind of quiet possibility. It didn’t need me to write in it. It was enough that it could be written in.

I’ve been thinking about how we create meaning out of empty spaces. A pause in a conversation can speak louder than words. A blank page can hold more than a full one. We tend to fear emptiness—of time, of ideas, of answers—but emptiness is also where invention lives. Before the first word, there is silence. Before the first step, there is stillness. And that silence and stillness are not failures. They are the raw material of everything we will become.

Language, too, is strange in this way. Every sentence we speak is a small act of selection from an infinite sea of possibilities. We cannot say everything. So we choose. And in choosing, we reveal what matters to us. The words we leave out are just as important as the words we put in. A good poem is made of its silences as much as its sounds. A good life, maybe, is made of the space we leave for the unexpected.

Tonight, I will close the notebook and put it back on the shelf. I won’t write in it. But I will carry it with me in a different way. It has already taught me something: that we don’t need to fill every blank space. Sometimes the most generous thing we can do is simply leave a page open, and wait for whatever wants to arrive.
